content: To prepare the sample, weigh it to the nearest milligram. Dissolve the sample by stirring it in the standard water used for testing, ensuring the final volume reaches the specified n milliliters. Store the resulting stock solution in a stoppered bottle until it is ready for use. To determine the volume (V ml) of the stock solution to be added to the test suspension of the water-dispersible granule, use the equation: V (ml) = (X × 1000) / (B × W) Where: B (g) is the weight of the emptied and cleaned bag. W (g) is the nominal weight of the water-dispersible granule (WG) contained in the bag. X (g) is the weight of the WG sample used in the test. For water-dispersible granules (WG), the sample mass used in the test should be specified at the highest rate recommended by the supplier. The test must be conducted in CIPAC standard water D unless another temperature or condition is specified. This method was officially adopted as a full CIPAC method in 2013. When measuring dustiness, the sample must be tested as received, ideally from a newly opened container, as changes in water content can significantly affect dustiness. If equipment is available, an alternative method showing good correlation with the gravimetric method may be used. However, in cases of doubt, the gravimetric method must be employed. For dissolution testing, the sampling of the bag should follow these steps: 1. Lay the empty, cleaned bag in its original double-layer configuration. 2. Delineate and cut a test sample, including part of the upper seal (5 cm) and symmetrically including the vertical seal (10 cm). If the bag size is smaller than these dimensions, use the entire bag. 3. Perform the dissolution test immediately to prevent any changes in the sample. Water-dispersible tablets (WT) are pre-formed solids of uniform shape and size, typically circular with flat or convex faces. They are designed for application after disintegration and dispersion in water using conventional spraying equipment. The formulation must be dry, free-flowing, and free from visible extraneous matter. The active ingredient must comply with identity tests, and additional tests may be required if the identity remains uncertain. Effervescent tablets, which incorporate an effervescent system, must disintegrate completely within a specified time. For wet sieve tests, a maximum percentage of material retained on a 75 µm sieve is allowed. Suspensibility tests require a minimum percentage of the formulation to remain in suspension after 30 minutes in CIPAC standard water D at 30 ± 2°C. Water-emulsifiable granules (EG) are formulations consisting of granules that form an oil-in-water emulsion upon disintegration and dissolution in water. These granules may contain active ingredients solubilized or diluted in an organic solvent, absorbed in a water-soluble polymeric shell or matrix. The formulation must be homogeneous, dry, free-flowing, and free from visible extraneous matter or hard lumps. Water-emulsifiable powders (EP) are applied as oil-in-water emulsions after dispersion in water. They contain active ingredients solubilized or diluted in organic solvents, absorbed in a water-soluble polymer powder or matrix. The formulation must be dry, free-flowing, and free from visible extraneous matter or hard lumps. Water-soluble powders (SP) are intended for application as true solutions of the active ingredient after dissolution in water. They may contain insoluble inert ingredients but must be free from visible extraneous matter and hard lumps. The dissolution of the bag containing the SP must be tested in CIPAC standard water D, and the degree of dissolution and solution stability must be evaluated. Water-soluble powders for seed treatment (SS) must be applied strictly according to the manufacturer’s recommendations to avoid adverse effects on germination. Treated seeds should be stored in suitable containers, protected from excessive temperature and moisture. The formulation must include a dye or pigment to color the seeds permanently after treatment, with red being the recommended color. Water-soluble granules (SG) must be homogeneous, free-flowing, and nearly dust-free. The active ingredient must be water-soluble, and the formulation must pass through a 5 mm sieve after 20 drops. Dustiness and attrition resistance must meet specified limits. For all formulations, methods of analysis must comply with CIPAC, AOAC, or equivalent standards. If unpublished methods are used, full details and validation data must be submitted to FAO/WHO.
